subject: Bryxton fintech - quant profile deploy caused p95/p99 latency regressions / exec attention
messages:
From: Sanjay Gupta <s.gupta@bryxton.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Bryxton NOC <noc@bryxton.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: p95/p99 jumps and 502s after update to v5alpha-q6_8

Marissa,

We started seeing a steep jump in p95/p99 latency at 08:12 PT and a cascade of 502/504s for our high-volume pay pipeline after your scheduled rollout. Throughput dropped ~35% and latency went from ~230ms p95 to ~1.4s p95 and 3.6s p99. Our fraud scoring flow is timing out and customers are hitting retries.

Attached is a short latency graph and our request IDs for the spike window. Can you confirm rollback and whether this is related to the new quant profile (q6_8) applied during the model switch? This is now impacting our checkout conversion. Our CTO wants an update in 30m.

— Sanjay
Bryxton Financial, Head of Platform
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Gupta <s.gupta@bryxton.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-25T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: p95/p99 jumps and 502s after update to v5alpha-q6_8

Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and the graphs. We've pulled initial logs. Early indicators point to a decoding stall pattern for v5alpha with the q6_8 quant profile under the customer’s peak prompt length distribution. Reproduced on our staging identical-load harness: p99 spike without obvious compute saturation.

Immediate actions:
- Rolling a targeted rollback of the model variant for Bryxton traffic to v4.11 (v4beta) starting now; expected propagation 6–8 minutes.
- Redirecting traffic through fallback routing policy to Dedicated pool A (lower batch slot) to reduce tail latency while rollback completes.
- Collecting artifact: deploy_manifest_v5alpha.json, customer_error_log_0625.txt (attached).

We will confirm when rollback is complete. If rollback resolves, next steps will be a fast postmortem on quant profile compatibility and a conservative re-test matrix.

— Marissa
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-25T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: triage notes & immediate mitigations (Bryxton)

Team — quick triage notes after initial rollback trigger. Repro summary:
- Model: v5alpha (encoder-decoder variant)
- Quant profile: q6_8 (aggressive weight quant+KV packing)
- Symptom: intermittent decode stalls causing token emission pauses + elevated 5xx rate under bursty traffic patterns (peak prompt lengths ~120–300 tokens)
- Staging reproduction: yes; p99 increases without CPU/GPU saturation; suggests kernel/code-path sensitivity to specific attention patterns and KV cache alignment.

Mitigations applied:
- Rollback to v4.11 for customer traffic (in flight).
- Temporary throttle on batch size for Bryxton route (max_batch_tokens = 1024).
- Enable experimental slow-path guard that forces synchronous decode for requests exceeding 180 tokens.

Asks for exec loop if rollback does not clear within 20m: we should prepare an outbound C-level note and discuss one-time credit or SLA concession. Captured artifacts and graphs in ticket SERV-1249.

— Rishi
Lead Inference Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Gupta <s.gupta@bryxton.com>, Alison Park <apark@bryxton.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Bcc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-25T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: p95/p99 jumps and 502s after update to v5alpha-q6_8

Sanjay / Alison — update:
- Rollback completed at 09:28 PT; we observe throughput recovering to normal levels and error rate down to baseline within the next 6 minutes.
- Attached: bryxton_p99_spike_20270625.png (before/after overlay).
- Short-term: we will keep Bryxton pinned to v4.11 for 24 hours while we run a targeted compatibility test matrix for q6_8 on your workload (prompt length distribution, multi-turn KV patterns).

Next steps we propose (for your approval):
1) Postmortem call today 16:00 PT — we’ll walk the timeline, root cause candidates, and corrective actions.
2) Optional: we can schedule a phased re-roll of v5alpha with a conservative quant profile (q8_6 fallback) and tighter canary rules.
3) Credit: if you prefer, we will prepare a goodwill credit for impacted window once we validate duration/impact.

Please confirm the 16:00 PT call or propose another slot. We’ll include our CSM and engineering leads.

— Marissa
From: Alison Park <apark@bryxton.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sanjay Gupta <s.gupta@bryxton.com>
Cc: Bryxton NOC <noc@bryxton.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-25T14:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: p95/p99 jumps and 502s after update to v5alpha-q6_8

Thanks — confirmed for 16:00 PT. The CTO will join. We appreciate the quick rollback and the temporary routing changes. On the call we want: clear root-cause hypothesis, timeline for mitigation coding work, and the credit calculation approach. Also please include testing artifacts so our SREs can review load reproduction steps.

— Alison
VP Infrastructure, Bryxton Financial
